terms.def: Applying for a green card without leaving the country.
A document that lets someone without a visa travel and come back. For TPS holders it is Form I-512T, and whether they ever used one can decide their whole case.
The government's decision that a country's conditions justify TPS. It has to be reviewed before it expires.
Employment Authorization Document. The work card. People call it "my papers."
An extension keeps TPS going for people who already have it. A redesignation also opens it to people who arrived more recently.
Whether someone was checked in at a border post when they entered. It sounds like paperwork. It decides whether they can get a green card without leaving.
The day a petition was filed. It is their place in line.
Immigration court. Run by the Justice Department, not by USCIS.
Ending a country's TPS. By law it cannot take effect less than 60 days after it is announced.
A clock that starts when status ends. Past certain points, leaving the country triggers a 3-year or 10-year bar on returning.
The gap between the announcement and the day it takes effect. It is notice, not extra benefits.

heading: Words you will hear
lede: If someone uses one of these, this is what they mean.
